A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MediRound work, and their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Corresponding main sections match reliably; v2 includes Appendices A–F, which are absent from the supplied v1.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–7 report original segmentation experiments, comparisons, and ablations on MR-MedSeg and SA-Med2D-20M.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by reference-input ablation results, dataset analyses, and additional qualitative examples in the appendix.

M1.justification: The architecture, conversation-history inputs, crop and bounding-box references, teacher forcing, and JCM inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendices A–B disclose training objectives and supervision details; they do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MR-MedSeg with the same five interaction scenarios, 168 categories, and nine modalities, plus SA-Med2D-20M evaluation. The appendix describes existing modalities and provides additional examples without establishing expanded task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged, including the human-guided and MLLM-assisted systems, SegLLM variants, and MediRound+READ. Table 4 specifies SAM as SAM (ViT-H), without establishing a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: Table A adds a controlled comparison using neither visual reference input, cropped images alone, and crops plus bounding boxes. Existing evaluation metrics, budgets, and splits remain unchanged; Table B's scenario counts sum to the split totals already reported in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a focused ablation of reference-mask information. Appendix D adds category-frequency analysis, and Figure C adds interactive case studies. The existing backbone and JCM-threshold ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance uncertainty estimates. The new dataset-frequency displays provide descriptive counts rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 swaps regular/hard-case entries for Qwen3-VL+IMIS-Net and Gemini-2.5-Pro+MediSee, and selected Dice/gIoU entries for SegLLM. Table 3 changes MedPLIB Dice/gIoU from 39.1/40.6 to 40.6/39.1. Table 4 revises the SAM row from 44.9/27.6/31.9 to 46.7/33.1/37.2, now labeled ViT-H. The appendix adds ablation scores, dataset findings, examples, and qualitative failure observations; MediRound's headline scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B newly specify the mathematical definitions of JCM's IoU-based soft supervision target and composite loss, together with MediRound's text-and-mask training objective. These are limited additions to the formal specification; the original inference equations remain unchanged and no proofs or theoretical guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about MEMR-Seg, the 177K-dialogue dataset, MediRound, and JCM's mitigation of error propagation. The added evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds substantial applicability limits: single-entity segmentation per turn, sensitivity to long queries, near-complete loss of general conversational capabilities, and inability to process 3D data or videos. It also attributes the reported weaknesses to sequence-length limitations and task-specific overfitting. These qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B supply previously missing training losses and JCM quality-target construction, substantially expanding implementation documentation. Appendix D, Table B, and Figure D add reference phrasing, modality names, scenario-level split statistics, and data examples. Appendix E.2 adds a future-release statement for the dataset and model; the existing project URL is retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 51 bibliography entries are unchanged. The appendix introduces no additional cited works.

P1.justification: The main prose and Sections 1–6 retain their wording and order. V2 appends an overview and organized explanatory Sections A–F, including expanded descriptions of existing interaction scenarios, rather than extensively rewriting the original narrative.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands visual documentation with a JCM training diagram, category-distribution displays, interactive prediction examples, and dataset samples in Figures A–D. Tables A–B add the reference-input ablation and detailed dataset composition. Existing main-text figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V1 refers readers to training and dataset details in an appendix that the supplied PDF lacks. V2 supplies central JCM supervision and training objectives, supporting analyses, and important capability limitations, substantially improving technical transparency and critical assessment. Table A's claim of best performance with both reference inputs overlooks crop-only's higher cIoU, 56.0 versus 55.8, but this limited overstatement does not outweigh the documentation gains.
